chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Early jobs to save for drums and starting on the peck horn
summary: Crawford says his school had no drum set, so he picked cotton and did odd jobs; he started on the peck horn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, this is more what I wanted to do, like now, where did you get your first -- first drum set or your first drums?
Well, the school I was going to, Stanley, they didn't have a drum set. So I just went out and worked. You know, I picked cotton when I was a kid, worked at

the cotton fields, I worked at a grocery store, delivering groceries, 30 cents a day, and on Saturdays I made 60 cents. So I just saved up hoping that I could. I'd give my grandmother, my grandparents what little change I could gather, press clothes, clean clothes with a brush, you know, scrub it, and odds and ends around the neighborhood, stack balls in a poolroom. You know, man, I did all kind of work just to try to go ahead. Now, anything else you'd like to ask me...
Yeah, now, like your first -- now, you -- one thing you -- now, you said at the school you went to they didn't have any drums.

No, they had -- I started out as a peck horn player. A peck horn, you know what that is? A peck horn is an English horn and straight up, you know, like a baritone, an old tuba. I started out as a peck horn.
